S16-R1: The panel will sit inside the asset card and be collapsed by default
S16-R2: Collapsed, it will carry a badge counting the services that are due soon, due today or overdue. It carries the badge alone, with no other text
S16-R3: Expanded, it lists every service that is due soon, due today or overdue, with covered services folded into the one that covers them where that service is also listed, and otherwise kept on rows of their own, and for a schedule with nothing due, that schedule's next service. Each row carries the summary of S16-R16
S16-R4: Every row shows when it is due in the words the asset tab uses, per S11-R9 and S11-R13
S16-R5: Rows carry the asset tab's badges, due soon, due today and overdue, with overdue in red. A compliance row is orange, never red, including when overdue, per S3-R10
S16-R6: A compliance row carries no tag. The service name alone identifies it, and the due date already says what it is
S16-R7: Hovering a service will show what it contains: job description, parts, and where one is attached the inspection form. At a location other than the home location the parts are headed PARTS CALGARY SOUTH USES (reference), because none of them will be added. On touch, tapping the service opens the same card
S16-R8: Add Service is a button on every row. It opens the Add Service modal, which offers this work order or a new one, per S17-R1
S16-R9: Add Service is available on every row whose service carries canned lines, including services not yet due. A service with no canned lines offers Mark complete alone, in the row's menu
S16-R10: A compliance certificate will be addable from the panel as well as from the asset
S16-R11: Where the asset is on no schedule, the panel offers Enroll in Schedule, opening the same modal as S7
S16-R12: Readings on a work order are entered in its existing Mileage and Engine Hours fields. Where one is missing, the service row reads Needs mileage reading, or Needs engine hours reading, and points to that field. The card opens no reading dialog of its own; once a reading is saved the panel shows what it moved, per S16-E1
S16-R13: Every row offers two ways to satisfy it: Add Service, which adds its canned lines to this work order, or at another location the same work per S16-N6, and resets the service when the work order is invoiced; and Mark complete, which resets it at once per S18-R6. Either marks the row addressed on this work order
S16-R14: Nothing infers a match from line text or canned lines. The advisor states that the work order satisfies a service; the system does not guess
S16-R15: A service whose lines were added resets when the work order is invoiced, through the step after invoicing. A service marked complete resets at once, per S18-R6
S16-R16: Each row reads as one summary, the line count and the hours, for example 4 lines · 2.8 hours, rather than listing its lines. It carries no money: no total on the row, in the hover card of S16-R7 or in the Add Service modal
S16-R17: Before a row's lines are added, Mark complete sits in the row's three-dot menu. Once Add Service has added them, the row reads Added · 4 lines and Mark complete takes Add Service's place as the row's button. Either way it opens the Mark complete modal of S18-R1 with this work order already chosen
S16-R18: A service marked addressed stays visible as such on the work order itself, not only in the audit log
S16-R19: Canned lines added for a service arrive the way canned lines arrive today, appended as separate, ordinary lines at the end of the work order. Nothing about nesting, grouping, line placement or the lines table changes for this feature: no parent line, no indent, no new column
S16-R20: The system records which service added which lines. The link is stored, not shown on the lines table; it appears in the panel, for example Added · 4 lines, and in the work order note of S17-R5
S16-R21: At a location other than the home location, the row reads exactly as it does at home, for example PM-A, Overdue · Aug 2026, 4 lines · 2.8 hours, Add Service, with an (i) beside it: PM-A's lines were set up at Calgary South. We add the same work here at Lethbridge's rates. Parts are not added; each line's note lists the parts Calgary South uses, for reference
S16-R22: Each copied line takes this location's labour type of the same name, or this location's default labour type where none matches, and is priced at that labour type's rate. A line that is fixed price at the home location is priced the same way here. A copied line carries the home line's tech time as well as its hours. A home line with no labour type is copied with none, so it is not priced, as at home
S16-R23: Each copied line carries its own internal line note, headed Line note · Internal, not visible to the customer, reading Copied from Calgary South. Parts used there, for reference: and then each part's quantity, name and part number, for example 2 × Rotella T4 15W-40, 18.9L · RT4-189. A fixed-price line's note reads Copied from Calgary South. Fixed price there, priced at Lethbridge's rate here
S16-R24: The Add Service modal is the standard one at every location. At a location other than the home location its preview lists no parts, because none are added; the card's (i) of S16-R21 is the only place that explains the copy
S16-R25: After Add Service a toast reads PM-A added · 4 lines, with Undo, for as long as the application's toasts stay. Once it is gone, the row's three-dot menu offers Remove, for an Add Service made by mistake, until the work order is invoiced. Undo and Remove do the same: the row returns to Add Service and is no longer addressed on this work order, so the step after invoicing does not list it. Neither deletes a line. The lines already added stay on the work order, as any line does, and are deleted by hand, per S16-N4, because a line's own state decides whether it can be deleted. Remove is not offered once the service has been reset, by Mark complete or by invoicing; Undo complete comes first, per S18-R17. Adding the service again after Undo or Remove re-attaches the lines still on the work order rather than adding them a second time, and adds only the lines no longer there
S16-N1: The panel carries no Enter a reading control of its own. Readings live above it, and an empty reading shows as needing one
S16-N2: Line search does not return maintenance services. Adding a line returns canned lines only
S16-N3: Nothing in the panel blocks closing the work order
S16-N4: Deleting the lines a service added does not unsatisfy that service. The advisor's statement governs, not which lines happen to remain
S16-N5: Nothing in the panel shows a price. An honest figure would need the customer's labour rate, tax, fees and discounts, which the work order itself already computes once the lines are on it
S16-N6: Add Service at a location other than the schedule's home location adds the same work, not the home location's lines: each canned line's name, description and hours, as new lines at this location's rates. Prices and parts are not copied, because both are kept per location. Tracking and completion stay organization-wide, per S18-R12
S16-N7: Add Service is not offered on a work order that is invoiced or paid, because adding lines there would void or reopen its invoice. The row's (i) reads Lines can't be created on an invoiced work order, and Mark complete stays in its menu
S16-N8: An organization with no maintenance schedule sees no maintenance card on a work order
S16-N9: An organization with one workplace never copies work. Every work order is at the home location
S16-E1: A reading entered here re-evaluates the unit immediately, and a service that has just become due says so. An In the shop value counts toward whether a meter threshold has been reached, so the service reads due at once. It changes neither the rate nor the confidence until it is recorded, per S10-R11
S16-E2: A unit with ten due services does not scroll forever, because the panel is collapsed by default
S16-E3: Splitting a work order keeps each service with the work order that carries its lines; a service marked complete stays with the original. Merging two assets moves their enrolments, readings, certificates and history to the asset that remains; where both were on the same schedule, the enrolment with the later completion stays
S17-R1: Adding from the work order card offers this work order or a new one. The worklist and the asset tab offer Create work order only, because neither has a current work order
S17-R2: Adding will bring the service's canned lines with it, or at another location the same work, per S16-N6
S17-R5: Adding writes one short internal work order note naming the service and the schedule it came from, for example PM-A added from Highway Tractor PM. It never mentions copying; each copied line's own note does, per S16-R23. The note is never visible to the customer, so it sends no customer email
S17-R6: Adding will write an audit entry with actor and timestamp
S17-R7: A service added from the worklist creates a work order and shows its number on the row
S17-R8: Canned lines duplicated across services will be deduplicated, so a unit never gets oil twice on one visit
S17-N1: Adding a service is permission gated and must offer the second destination, because a technician with three hours left cannot take on ten more lines
S17-N2: A declined estimate resets nothing. The service stays due and stays on the list
S17-E1: A shop that writes PM-A as one four hour line and a shop that writes it as four canned lines must both be possible
S17-E2: An existing work order whose lines were typed by hand must be able to satisfy a due service without re-adding the lines
S17-E3: A declined estimate later approved and completed advances the schedule. The completion decides, not the path taken to it
S18-R1: Mark complete sits in the row's three-dot menu on the asset tab, on the worklist and on the maintenance card of a work order. On a work order card row whose lines were added it is the row's button instead, per S16-R17. Its (i) reads: Resets this service now, from the date you choose. It won't wait for an invoice. Every place opens the same modal, titled for the service, for example Mark PM-A complete, with one line under the title: PM-A resets now from the date below. It won't wait for an invoice
S18-R2: Where was it done? offers On a work order or Completed elsewhere. On a work order lists work orders by number, location, date and status, from any location in the organization. Opened from a work order card, that work order is already chosen
S18-R3: Reset date is always shown and is never in the future. For a work order not yet invoiced it defaults to today. For an invoiced work order it defaults to the day the service's lines were all closed, otherwise the invoice date, with both offered beneath the field, for example Lines closed 4 Sep · Use invoice date (1 Oct)
S18-R4: Completed elsewhere asks optionally for the shop's name and a reading. Its Reset date has no default and is required
S18-R5: On a compliance service the modal also takes the certificate: number, Start date, End date and term, per S8-R10. Start date defaults to the Reset date, End date fills in from it plus the term, and both can be changed
S18-R6: Mark complete resets the service at once from its Reset date, on either branch. It never waits for an invoice. A service whose lines were added instead, and not marked complete, waits for its work order's invoice: until then its worklist row reads the work order's Complete status with its Invoice action, per S13-R26
S18-R7: Covered services reset with the one that covers them, each on its own interval. They are shown as a consequence of that service rather than as rows of their own, with one date to correct and not five
S18-R8: The step after invoicing lists every service whose lines were added on this work order, each ticked by default and can be unticked, with its reason, for example Lines added from PM-A. An unticked service does not reset and stays due. A service already reset by Mark complete is not listed: a service resets once
S18-R9: Each closed line will stamp the date it closed, visible on the work order and distinct from the invoice date
S18-R10: A service added by its canned lines completes when every line it added completes. A service marked complete without lines completes when it is marked. The spec means line completion by any of the five paths that reach it: completing the line, the bulk action bar, creating an invoice, clocking out, and review
S18-R11: Completion will record where it happened, including another shop
S18-R12: Completion travels across the organization. A unit serviced at one location advances what another location tracks
S18-R13: Where a work order added the lines of one or more maintenance services, invoicing it shows each of those services with the date its cycle counts from. The date proposed is when that service's own lines were all closed, which S18-R9 stamps, and the invoice date only where there is nothing better. Every path that closes a line stamps that date: completing the line, the bulk action bar, creating an invoice, clocking out and review. Where a path leaves no date, the invoice date is proposed
S18-R14: The proposed date is editable and names the day the work was done. The next due follows from it through the service's own interval and updates as it changes, so a shop invoicing weeks late resets from the work rather than from the paperwork
S18-R15: Accepting every proposed date is one action, Confirm dates. A shop that invoices on the day of the work passes through without touching it, and closing the step without touching it accepts every proposal too, per S18-N5
S18-R16: The same step carries a Compliance certificates section for every compliance service on this work order, one record per inspection: type, number, Start date, End date and term, where Start date plus the term fills End date per S8-R10. The section is optional
S18-R17: After Mark complete a toast reads PM-A marked complete · next due counts from 2 Oct 2026, with Undo. The row reads Completed · next due counts from 2 Oct 2026, and its menu offers Undo complete until the service's next cycle moves again. On the worklist the row leaves the list and returns when its next cycle reads due soon, per S13-R43
S18-R18: A service whose schedule was removed from the asset while its work order was open is not listed in the step after invoicing and does not reset
S18-R19: Mark complete On a work order also records that work order's mileage and engine hours as the asset's readings, dated the Reset date, exactly as invoicing would per S10-R10, where S10-N6 counts them as readings. A fleet that never invoices its own trucks keeps both its services and its readings current this way
S18-R20: The step comes straight after the invoice is created and before the payment dialog, because paying reloads the page and a step shown after it would be lost
S18-R21: Closing the step after changing a date asks: Discard your changes? The proposed dates stay. Closing it without changing anything accepts every proposal, per S18-R15
S18-N1: The completion step is skippable. Nothing blocks closing a work order
S18-N2: A work order that is never invoiced never resets a service whose lines it added. The shop resets it with Mark complete, per S18-R1
S18-N3: Completion must work with no canned line involved anywhere, because many shops type every line freeform
S18-N4: Nothing scolds. A shop typing freeform is not doing anything wrong
S18-N5: The step appears only where a maintenance service was completed. It never appears on an ordinary work order, and leaving without touching it accepts every proposal, on the same rule as S18-N1
S18-N6: Completing a work order shows no maintenance step. Everything happens in the step after invoicing
S18-N7: The step is shown to every user who can invoice. It needs no other permission, because it only confirms when the work was done
S18-N8: The step cannot be reopened, and nothing offers to change its dates afterwards. The date confirmed there is the date the service counts from, and the service reads as done
S18-E1: Early completion is normal. Fleets move compliance work months earlier to fit a slow season, and nothing warns or confirms
S18-E2: Reversing an invoice deletes it in ShopView, and closing an unpaid invoice's payment dialog reverses it seconds after invoicing. The resets that invoice made are undone, and its services are proposed again when the work order is next invoiced, keeping any date a person entered. A credit memo changes nothing
S18-E3: A pending invoice that ShopView voids because a line was added to its work order is treated the same way: its services are proposed again when the work order is next invoiced
S18-E4: A work order closing two compliance inspections asks for details per record
S18-E5: The system cannot detect work done elsewhere and does not try. The reminder is what prompts the customer to mention it
S18-E6: A compliance inspection is not in the step's list of dates. Its next due comes from the certificate's End date per S12-R4, entered in the certificate section of S18-R16
S18-E7: A fleet shop that never invoices its own work orders keeps every schedule current with Mark complete alone
S18-E8: A truck serviced on Monday and invoiced three weeks later is marked complete on Monday and counts its next cycle from Monday. The worklist shows nothing due for it in between, and invoicing later changes nothing
S10-R1: The reading dialog will be the same component from the asset and from the work order
S10-R2: It will show current on the left, read only with its source and age, and new on the right
S10-R4: A reading will carry a timestamp and an author
S10-R5: Saving will re-evaluate every dependent threshold immediately, not overnight
S10-R10: Every change to an asset's mileage or engine hours is stored as a dated reading with its source: work order, asset, customer portal, import or API. A value on an open work order shows In the shop until that work order is invoiced, per S10-R11. The last value entered is the current reading, even when it is lower; a lower value is flagged and both stay in history
S10-R11: A reading entered on an open work order shows as In the shop rather than recorded, until that work order is invoiced. The invoice is what fixes it, per S10-R10, so between the two there is a value the shop can see and the history does not yet carry. Mark complete on that work order fixes it too, per S18-R19, so a fleet that never invoices its own trucks still builds a reading history
S10-R12: At release, the mileage and engine hours on every past work order and in imported history are loaded once as dated readings, with their source, so an organization's estimates work from its first day. From release, readings are recorded for every organization
S10-R6: Distance and engine hours will each have their own row
S10-R7: An undo will appear after saving
S10-R8: A wrong reading is corrected by entering the right one: the last value entered is the current reading, per S10-R10, and both values stay in the audit, per S21-R4
S10-R9: The field reads Mileage. Where a value names its unit it reads mileage in full, never mi or km
S10-N1: No reading value is ever rejected by validation
S10-N2: An implausible value shows an orange, plainly worded confirmation and saves on confirm. Never red, never blocking. The same figures as S11-R19 decide what is implausible: more than 1,500 mileage a day, or more than 24 engine hours a day, since the last reading
S10-N3: A value lower than the last one saves, is flagged, and both values stay in history
S10-N4: The reading modal forecasts nothing. Saving returns to the maintenance tab, which already shows every service the reading moved, with room to show it properly
S10-N5: There is no live telematics feed in v1. Every reading is entered by a person or taken from a work order, which is why no projected figure is ever printed as a fact
S10-N6: A reading on a work order counts only when someone entered or changed the value on that work order. The mileage a new work order copies from the asset is not a reading, so a work order nobody read the meter on never makes a unit look freshly read. Work orders created from the worklist copy mileage like any other
S10-E1: A gauge and an ECU legitimately disagree. If the gauge was ever replaced they cannot be synced
S10-E2: A replacement engine resets the hours. A 2019 unit showing 11 engine hours is expected the week after a swap
S10-E3: A correction recomputes the rate from stored pairs and moves every threshold and queued reminder
S10-E4: Two readings on the same day: the rate takes the higher one. Display keeps the last entered
S11-R1: An estimate will be the last recorded reading carried forward at a computed rate
S11-R2: The rate is what the meter added across the unit's last three usable pairs, divided by the days those pairs span: the three intervals are added together and read as one period. Older pairs are not used. With one or two usable pairs, all of them are used. A newer interval counts more simply because only the latest ones are taken
S11-R3: Readings from imported history and from work orders will both be used
S11-R4: Pairs less than seven days apart will be discarded
S11-R5: Pairs where the reading did not increase will be discarded
S11-R6: Readings dated in the future or in an impossible year will be discarded before anything runs
S11-R7: The rate will never be cached incrementally. A correction anywhere in the history recomputes it
S11-R8: Confidence will be one of Low, Medium, High. It grades an estimate, and is deliberately not the vocabulary used for a reading's own state in S9-R2
S11-R9: Every estimated due date shows a month, at every confidence, with its confidence beneath it as the meter and a word: High, Medium or Low confidence. The rule that produced it, for example based on mileage estimate, sits in the meter's hover. A due or overdue service shows its badge and still its month. An exact date belongs to a recorded reading alone
S11-R17: No data is a separate state, not a confidence level. It applies where there is nothing to estimate from, the calendar governs, and the row says the meter has no basis yet
S11-R10: Distance and engine hours will each carry their own confidence, computed independently
S11-R11: Every projected value will name the rule that produced it: based on mileage, based on engine hours, based on the certificate term, based on the calendar
S11-R12: Estimated distance will round to the nearest 100 and estimated hours to the nearest 10. A recorded reading is shown exactly as entered
S11-R18: A rate will read as an accrual without naming a unit, for example 640 a week. The word mileage describes a unit's history, not a speculative rate, so it does not appear here
S11-R19: A pair producing a rate above 1,500 mileage a day, or above 24 engine hours a day, is discarded for rate purposes. The reading itself is kept and shown; nothing is refused at entry. Nothing in the application classifies units, so one ceiling applies to every unit
S11-R20: A pair whose two readings sit more than a year apart is not used for a rate. It averages across too long a span to describe what the unit is doing now
S11-R21: The complete matrix ships with the specification as one table for the build, directly beneath these requirements: readings counted, age of the last reading, the confidence that follows, and what the row renders. The rules are spread across S11 and S12 and an engineer needs them side by side
S11-R22: Confidence comes from one table that reads two things together: how old the unit's last recorded reading is, and how many usable pairs it has. Every combination has its own cell, given in S11-R24 and in the table beneath these requirements. Nothing is graded separately and nothing caps anything
S11-R23: A usable pair is two consecutive readings that survive the guards in S11-R4, S11-R5, S11-R19 and S11-R20, after S11-R6 has removed impossible readings. Only readings from the last 24 months count, per S11-R26. No usable pair is No data. In a clean history one pair is two visits, two or three pairs are three or four visits, and four or more pairs are five or more visits. Where a guard discards a pair the count drops with it
S11-R24: By age of the last recorded reading, then usable pairs. Up to 30 days: one pair Medium, two or more High. 31 to 90 days: one pair Low, two or three Medium, four or more High. 91 to 180 days: one pair Low, two or more Medium. 181 to 365 days: four or more Medium, fewer Low. Over 365 days: Low. A value shown In the shop per S10-R11 is not yet recorded and does not refresh the age until its work order is invoiced
S11-R25: Measured from N visits, where a card shows it, counts the readings that took part in at least one usable pair. A visit whose only pairs were discarded does not count
S11-R26: Readings older than 24 months are not used, for the rate or for the pair count. A unit whose readings are all older than that reads No data and the calendar governs, as for a unit never read
S11-R27: The meter's hover ends with: This is the system's best estimate from this unit's past readings. Check its history if in doubt. Beside it, View work orders opens the asset's Work Orders tab
S11-R13: An overdue row derived from a meter estimate shows its estimated month and carries no figure at any confidence: never overdue by 1,200 mileage. A date from a certificate reads its End date and Certificate, for example 14 Oct 2026 · Certificate, because the certificate names the day. A date from the calendar reads its month and Calendar
S11-R14: A rate is measured from the unit's own readings and from nothing else. Without a usable pair there is no rate and no estimate: the calendar carries the service and the row says the meter has no basis yet. Comparing a meter against itself holds whichever distance unit a shop counts in, which a supplied figure cannot
S11-N1: In Low, a reminder sent by hand shows Soon rather than a month, per S19-R9. The advisor may prefer to call
S11-N2: In No data the meter produces no candidate at all and does not compete
S11-N3: No date is ever presented as fact when it is a projection
S11-E1: No data is the ordinary state. Four units in five have no meter basis, and the UI must not treat it as missing data
S11-E2: One usable pair, which is two visits in a clean history, is the floor at which anything is computed
S11-E4: Engine hours will sit in Low and No data far more often than distance, because hours are recorded on roughly one visit in six
S11-E5: Two visits, the last one yesterday: one pair, under 30 days, Medium. Six visits, five pairs, the last reading 120 days old: Medium. Twelve visits over three years, the last one eight months ago: Medium. The same unit fourteen months after its last visit: Low. Every reading older than 24 months: No data, and the calendar governs
S11-E6: June to July adds 2,700 in 30 days, July to September 6,000 in 60 days, September to October 3,000 in 30 days: 11,700 in 120 days, a rate of 97.5 a day. The unit last read 345,700 and the next service is at 360,000, so 14,300 remain, about 147 days, and the service is due in March. Its confidence comes from the table in S11-R24, not from this sum
S12-R1: Every active trigger will propose a candidate date
S12-R2: The calendar always proposes one. A meter in No data proposes nothing
S12-R3: A service set "At" a reading comes due when the unit reaches it and stays overdue until it is done; once done, it never comes due again. A service set "At" a day of the year comes due on that day each year and stays overdue until it is done; next year's date appears only once it is done. Doing it early or late does not move next year's date
S12-R4: A compliance service is due on its current certificate's End date. It reads due soon from its Remind before expiry, due today on that day and overdue from the next day
S12-R5: Due will be the earliest candidate
S12-R6: Confidence will change how the date is rendered, never which candidate wins
S12-R7: Within one service, its triggers' candidates resolve to the earliest per S12-R5. The Due cell shows that one with its trigger per S9-R12, and the row menu lists every other candidate with its date and trigger. Rows are never merged across services on the asset tab, the worklist or the panel
S12-R8: Where two triggers of one service land on the same day, the Due cell names the one with the higher confidence
S12-R9: Grouping services into one entry applies to the customer email alone, in S19. On the asset tab, the worklist and the panel every service keeps its own row
S12-R10: Covering is what a shop states per S2-R16, never inferred from interval length or shared lines. Within one schedule a service covers the services it names. Across schedules nothing is covered
S12-R11: Covered services reset with the one that covers them, each on its own interval
S12-R12: Canned lines will be deduplicated by identity, so a unit never gets oil twice on one visit
S12-R13: A compliance inspection is never covered
S12-R14: Today is the day of the location the user is working in, as chosen in the header, which already sets the timezone for the session. A due-today row resolves against it.
S12-N1: A meter with no usable delta is silent rather than wrong
S12-N2: The row menu never hides a candidate
S12-E1: A reset moves every candidate on that service at once, anchored on the date confirmed per S18-R13
S12-E2: An "At" date does not move when the service is done early or late
S12-E3: A new reading recalculates candidates immediately
S12-E4: A unit on two schedules with the same service produces two rows and one phone call
S12-E5: Where a work order is invoiced, the reading is recorded first and the cycle resets second, so the reading carried forward is the one at invoicing
S19-R1: One email will exist. Send reminder on the contact card sends it for one asset, per S14-R6. Nothing sends it automatically in v1
S19-R2: The wording the dialog opens with is fixed and the same for every shop. It is phrased so it holds for any mix of states and never needs a singular and a plural form
S19-R3: Send reminder opens the application's existing send email dialog. Its recipients are the customer's contacts, each with a checkbox. The asset's preferred contact is ticked where it has an email address. A contact without one is listed unticked, cannot be ticked, and shows No email with Add email, which adds the address to that contact so it can then be ticked. The dialog's field takes further addresses
S19-R4: The dialog's content box is prefilled with the wording of S19-R2 and can be changed for that one send, as in every email sent from that dialog. Beneath it the reminder table for the asset is read only. There is no wording editor for the shop, per S19-N7
S19-R5: An asset with one service due today and another overdue gets one email listing both. The table carries the state per row
S19-R6: An email carries every service of the asset that the worklist shows: overdue, due today and due within the next 91 days, per S13-R36, whatever state each one is in
S19-R7: Where none is, it carries the asset's next two upcoming services, each as Coming up, so Send reminder always has something to send and is never disabled for having nothing due. Nothing beyond those is included
S19-R8: Each row in the email names the unit, the service where known, when it is due and its state: Past due, Due today or Coming up
S19-R9: Each row shows its due month where the date is sound. Where a row's date would be a guess, including every Low confidence date, it reads Soon rather than a month the shop would be held to. The email never shows confidence wording
S19-R14: Every send is recorded in the audit with the message, the recipients, the user who sent it and the timestamp, per S21-R5, and updates Last sent on the contact card, per S14-R12. Today only invoice and estimate emails are recorded, on their work order, so this record is new
S19-R15: The footer will state why the customer received it. There is no unsubscribe link: consent is managed by a setting on the customer record, not by a link in the mail
S19-R16: The layout and the wording will be hardcoded, populated from shop and asset data, and will follow the existing ShopView send pattern
S19-R17: The email is sent as the organization's name over the platform sending address, the same pattern the invoice and purchase order emails already use. ShopView's own address never shows as the sender's name
S19-R18: Reply-To is the user who pressed Send, as on the invoice and purchase order emails. The dialog's toggle to include their own email sends them a copy as BCC
S19-R19: The email opens with the first and last name of the person it goes to, for example Hi Dave Brabay. With two people ticked it names both, Hi Dave Brabay and Lisa Brabay; with three or more, or where no ticked address carries a name, it reads Hello. The signature is the one the invoice email already carries: Best regards, the user's name, the organization's name and the telephone of the location chosen in the header. The call to action is to call. Booking is a conversation, and a telephone is present where an email address often is not. An address typed in the dialog's field does not change the greeting
S19-R21: Where the location has no telephone, the call to action is omitted rather than printed with nothing after it
S19-R23: Where the unit has nothing dated at all, for example its only service is a compliance inspection with no certificate, or every service is skipped, the opening line and the table give way to Nothing is scheduled for 402 yet. The call to action and the signature stay
S19-N3: A customer whose notification setting is off cannot be sent a reminder for any of their assets, per S14-R9. The setting lives on the customer record, not on the asset and not on the enrolment
S19-N5: There is no internal email. Every message v1 sends goes to a customer
S19-N7: There is no wording editor in Settings, no subject the shop can change and no reset to default. Those are a later version. Changing the content of one send in the dialog is not an editor
S19-N8: The send reuses the work order send mechanism as it stands: the dialog, the organization as sender over the platform address, and the reply address of the user who pressed Send
S19-E4: Bounces are not tracked. Nothing will report that a reminder failed to arrive
S22-R1: A work order carries the origin when it was created from a due service, or when Add Service added a service to it
S22-R2: The Work Orders list will gain a Maintenance schedule column, naming the schedule and linking to it where the work order came from one. Where the user cannot open the schedule, its name shows as plain text, without a link
S22-R3: The column will be empty for work orders with no maintenance origin
S22-R4: The Work Orders list gains a From maintenance filter. With it applied, a line above the list reads the count and the total of every matching work order across all pages, for example 42 work orders · $38,410 · Work order total. The total is each work order's own total, not only the lines a service added. An organization-wide revenue report follows later
S22-N1: A work order created by hand carries no origin and is not inferred into one
S22-N2: Open rates and bounce reporting are not tracked
S22-N3: Mark complete is not an origin. It creates no work order and adds nothing to one
S22-E1: A service added to an existing work order marks that work order's origin without replacing an origin it already had
S22-E2: Without this column there is no way to answer whether the feature earned anything, which is why it is v1 rather than later
